source.excerpt: Friends have all things in common.
trail: Wikiquote connects this English wording with Diogenes Laertius VIII.10. The checked Hicks transcription says “Friends have all things in common” and attributes the report to Timaeus. This is ancient testimony about Pythagoras, not his surviving manuscript. Saying and reference ↗
Section ten reports the saying through Timaeus, with a different English formulation. Diogenes’ testimony ↗

author.heading: About Pythagoras
author.bio: Pythagoras was an ancient Greek thinker associated with a philosophical and religious community. The surviving evidence about him is later and often difficult to separate from the traditions of his followers.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Diogenes Laertius reports communal friendship as a Pythagorean principle through an earlier historical source. That is ancient testimony about a tradition, rather than a surviving text written by Pythagoras himself.
